name: Arnarstapi to Hellnar coastal path
region: Arnarstapi and Hellnar nature reserve, Snæfellsnes
why: Along the old Neðstagata track over a 3,900-year-old lava field, past sea arches and basalt gorges full of kittiwakes, to a fishing hamlet with a café on the beach.
book: Free, no permit. Park in Arnarstapi by the harbour. Camping in the reserve is not allowed.
water: Nothing on the path; cafés and toilets in Arnarstapi and at Fjöruhúsið in Hellnar.
dangers: Unfenced cliff edges above the surf: keep to the marked path, above all in wind.
Arctic terns nesting at Arnarstapi dive at walkers in June and July: wear a hat and keep moving.
turnaround: In a storm with spray over the cliffs, walk only to Gatklettur and back.

points.name: Gatklettur arch, Arnarstapi
points.note: The sea arch below the harbour cliffs, a few minutes from the car park and Bárður's stone statue. Snæfellsjökull stands behind the village.

points.name: Hellnahraun lava coast
points.note: Halfway: the track crosses the mossy lava close to the cliffs, with sea caves and stacks below. Draugarlág cave is by the path.

points.name: Hellnar beach and Baðstofa cave
points.note: An old fishing port of 200 people in the 1600s, now a few houses, a small church and the Fjöruhúsið café by the beach. Baðstofa sea cave is in the rocks east of the cove.
